reason: MA-WAM uses a world-action model to generate/rank candidate multi-agent trajectories at test time. Reported planning can improve task returns over reactive policies, but uses up to eight candidate rollouts; its cost discussion concerns world-model test-time planning, not LLM inference/serving or reducing compute. It evaluates coordination benchmarks rather than LLM workloads; benefits are limited near the task ceiling and experiments use M=8/horizon cap 8.
title: MA-WAM: Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Test-Time Planning
